sections.title: Adults-only sign-up gate
sections.what: Checks that the sign-up form explains the adults-only rule, keeps the submit button disabled until the age box is ticked, and then sends the user on to onboarding. It also checks the server refuses a sign-up without the confirmation.
sections.why: Enforces the age rule on both the visible form and the server, so one cannot be bypassed by the other.
sections.watch_out: The server test relies on a fixed client address header, so rate limits can make it fail on repeat runs.

summary: Browser and API tests that check the sign-up page requires adults-only confirmation before a new account is created.
purpose: Confirms the 18-plus beta gate works in the screen and in the server.
why: The beta is for adults only, so both the form and the server must refuse sign-ups without the confirmation.
how: The first test opens the sign-up page, checks the adults-only notice is shown, fills in the form, and confirms the submit button stays disabled until the age box is ticked. After ticking it, the test expects a move to onboarding. The second test sends a sign-up straight to the API without the age confirmation and expects a 400 response with a message about being aged 18 and over.
inputs: A made-up name, a unique email built from the current time, a password, and a fake client address header.
outputs: Pass or fail results for the form gate and the server gate.
risks: The fake client address header is set to a fixed value, so repeated runs can hit sign-up rate limits.
debug: If the button never enables, check the age checkbox label. If the API test fails, check the server's refusal message and status code.
